clue.text: Pools entries making one a rich man

definitions.meaning: plunges into swimming pools are headfirst entries into the water
the rich man in the parable of Lazarus is traditionally named ...

explanation.surface: Someone wins big on the football pools and becomes wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pools' suggests the British football pools, a betting coupon; here it means swimming pools. 'making' is the link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is a plunge into water, and the Latin word for rich gave the biblical wealthy man his traditional name.

clue.text: Ruthless sort of canine activity?

parts.note: read literally, hounds devouring each other; idiomatically, fiercely competitive

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes cut-throat competition where rivals destroy each other.

clue.text: Rockets — or what one has to face in combat

definitions.text: what one has to face in combat

parts.note: the V-1 was a German flying bomb, so several of them are V1s, written with I for 1
taken as written

explanation.surface: In wartime, a soldier faces rocket attacks or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: V1s were German wartime flying bombs; the 1 is read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable front of a helmet covers a fighter's face.

clue.text: Rage after vessels capsized in Scandinavian port

indicators.note: the word for rage follows the turned vessels
in a down clue the vats are turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: vats are large containers for liquid
rage means anger

explanation.surface: Fury erupts when boats overturn in a Norwegian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns VATS to STAV, and 'after' puts ANGER behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a harbour city in south-west Norway.

clue.text: Make arrangement for leaf to die

definitions.text: Make arrangement for leaf to die

indicators.note: making an arrangement of the next words tells us to reorder their letters

explanation.surface: Someone plans for foliage to wither and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make arrangement for' rearranges LEAFTODIE; the whole clue is also the definition, since stripping a plant of leaves is arranging for them to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip trees of foliage is to cause their leaves to wither and fall, as with chemical sprays.

clue.text: Put up (likewise down) for the Pantheon

definitions.text: Put up (likewise down) for the Pantheon

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same written upwards as downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone is elevated to join the gods in the Pantheon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' means read upward in this down entry, and 'likewise down' says it reads the same both ways; being put up for the Pantheon is being made a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised to the status of a god, as Roman emperors were.

clue.text: Originally, in fact, a mad religious type

indicators.note: mad tells us these letters are jumbled crazily into another order

explanation.surface: In its original sense the word described a crazed religious devotee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges INFACTA. 'Originally' nods to the Latin root, meaning inspired by a temple god.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot driven by extreme religious enthusiasm.

clue.text: Give the wall to French primate

parts.note: le is French for the
mur is French for wall

explanation.surface: Someone yields right of way at the wall to a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to French' asks for 'the wall' in French: le mur.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-dwelling Madagascan animal with a long tail, of the same order as apes.

clue.text: This circle could be intact with part of circumference put in

indicators.note: the segment is put inside the rearranged letters
the word intact could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: an arc is a section of a circle's circumference

explanation.surface: Geometry: a circle stays intact when a segment is inserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges INTACT into ANTTIC, and 'put in' places ARC inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of latitude round the South Pole, about 66.5 degrees south.

clue.text: Result's equal, to a T

parts.note: even means level or equal

explanation.surface: A match ends in a precisely level score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' adds the letter T after EVEN; the phrase also means exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or occurrence; a happening.

clue.text: Position after middle of August, in a sense

indicators.note: the word for position comes after the letters from the month
the middle three letters of the month's name are taken from inside it

parts.note: a station is a post or position someone occupies

explanation.surface: Someone describes a post taken up in mid-August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central letters of AUGUST, and 'after' places STATION behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, and its formal name is this.

clue.text: Order of Merit for head of church

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new order is signalled, disguised as the British honour the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone is awarded the Order of Merit for leading the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour; here 'Order of' asks for the letters of MERIT to be reordered. 'for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed ceremonial hat is worn on the head by a leading churchman.

clue.text: A legal examination cut short in Roman courts

indicators.note: the word for the legal examination loses its final letter, being cut short

parts.note: a trial is the examination of a case in a court of law

explanation.surface: A court hearing in Rome is abandoned partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final L of TRIAL to give TRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the open central court of a Roman house.

clue.text: Explain how to help international understanding

definitions.meaning: to make clear the meaning of something
translating between languages helps foreign parties understand each other

explanation.definitionFit: To expound something is to make it clear, and translating speech for foreign listeners is the second sense.

clue.text: Does he err as much as he forgives?

definitions.text: Does he err as much as he forgives?

parts.words: Does he err as much as he forgives?
parts.note: alludes to the saying that to err is human and to forgive divine: a being half mortal and half god would do both equally

explanation.walkthrough: Pope's line 'To err is human, to forgive divine' makes erring the human half and forgiving the divine half of a part-god.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-divine figure of myth, like Hercules, is partly mortal and partly a god.

clue.text: General assistant to cook, say, in work unit'

indicators.note: the sound of the cooking word goes inside the work unit

parts.note: a man-day is a unit of one person's work for a day

indicators.note: say means the word for cook is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat

explanation.surface: An all-purpose helper is put to cooking in a work team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns FRY into FRI by sound, and 'in' places it inside MANDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe's servant gave his name to any loyal all-round helper.

clue.text: I. for example, accumulated wealth

definitions.meaning: the letter I written large is an upper-case letter
money and assets amassed for investment

explanation.surface: Someone talks about themselves as an example of riches piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper-case letter and stored-up money for investment share this one word.

clue.text: Unisex type eats short measure of fruit

annotationWithheld.why: Unisex type eats short measure of fruit: PERSON round IMM gives the answer, but no reading of 'short measure' yields IMM
annotationWithheld.clue: Unisex type eats short measure of fruit

clue.text: Chap takes daring trip in Russia

parts.note: Len is a man's name, so a chap

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, signalling that the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A man makes a bold journey through Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges DARING into INGRAD after LEN; 'takes' links. Leningrad was the Soviet name of St Petersburg.
explanation.definitionFit: Soviet-era name of St Petersburg, a city there.

clue.text: Catholic? Monk, for example

definitions.meaning: catholic in its lower-case sense means universal or wide-ranging
George Monck, often spelt Monk, was the army commander who restored Charles II

explanation.surface: Asks whether a monk counts as a Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letters on 'Catholic' and 'Monk' suggest the church; they are the adjective universal and the seventeenth-century commander George Monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal or broad matches the lower-case adjective, and Monk held top military rank in the English Civil War era.

clue.text: Recent arrival's kit still delayed outside

indicators.note: the word for delayed goes outside the other

parts.note: late means delayed
yet means still, as in not yet

explanation.surface: A baby's things are still held up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps LATE round YET; the 'recent arrival' is a newborn baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of clothes and bedding for a newborn baby.

clue.text: A French one is able to provide this violet

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is able to supply a certain flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide this' links wordplay to definition; the violet is the African violet, a common houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: The saintpaulia houseplant is popularly called the African violet.

clue.text: Prepare to drive from where one lives

definitions.meaning: in golf, to settle the club behind the ball before a stroke

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer lines up behind the ball before striking it, and a home's location is also given by this word.

clue.text: Made picture of Dieppe operation, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the 1942 Allied attack on the French harbour of Dieppe was a port raid

explanation.surface: Someone painted a scene of the wartime attack on Dieppe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dieppe Raid of 1942 was an Allied assault on a French harbour; 'port raid', spoken, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict in a painting or drawing is to make a picture of someone.

clue.text: Fair maid from here — Catharine or Sheila?

definitions.text: Fair maid from here — Catharine or Sheila?

parts.words: Fair maid from here — Catharine or Sheila?
parts.note: Scott's novel The Fair Maid of the Scottish city has heroine Catharine Glover; Sheila is Australian slang for a woman, pointing to the Western Australian city of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Two cities share the name: one in Scotland (Scott's Fair Maid) and one in Western Australia, where a sheila is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Scotland and the capital of Western Australia share this name.

clue.text: She may -find love hard to arrange

indicators.note: the letters of the pieces are set out in a new order

parts.note: in tennis scoring love means zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman finds romance difficult to organise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' reorders O (love) and HARD; 'may find' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a female.

clue.text: Nibs enough to 'supply writer?

indicators.note: the letters are supplied from within the run of the words nibs enough

explanation.surface: Asks whether pen nibs are enough to equip an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to supply' draws the letters from inside 'nIBS ENough'; the writer is the Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian dramatist, author of A Doll's House.

clue.text: Flanks partially taken

definitions.meaning: the ... of a body or an army
to take ... is to be partial in a dispute

explanation.definitionFit: Flanks are the lateral parts of something, and biased people take these in an argument.

clue.text: Sort of communication that's read is now totally pointless

indicators.note: every compass point letter, north, south, east and west, is taken away from the phrase

explanation.surface: A message reads as if it has become completely meaningless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totally pointless' removes all four compass points E, S, N and W from READISNOW, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting by electromagnetic waves is a form of communication.

clue.text: Article King Midas' as turned to gold this month

parts.note: the is the definite article
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: one part of the word is changed into something else, as Midas turned things

parts.note: taken as written
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The legendary king turns things to gold in a certain month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned to' changes the AS in MIDAS into OR (gold), giving MIDOR. The month is the eleventh of the French Revolutionary calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Revolutionary calendar named its summer month of heat this.

clue.text: Hits farmworkers

definitions.meaning: people who cut and dry grass for fodder

explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a wild swinging punch, and also a labourer who cuts and turns grass for fodder.

clue.text: Pushed on to sign agreement about state's borders

indicators.note: the word for the gesture goes around the other letters

parts.note: to nod the head is to signal agreement

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone was pressured into signing an accord about frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes S and E, the first and last letters of 'state's', and 'about' puts NOD round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward cautiously, as a car or boat does, is to push ahead slowly.
